lines.description: The invoice lines to adjust. Leave out a line to leave it alone; leave out an amount to credit the whole of what is left on the line.

creditAmount.description: How much of the line to credit, as a decimal.

creditQuantity.description: The quantity credited, as a decimal.

description.description: The line's wording on the credit memo, when it should differ.

invoiceLineId.description: The line's id, from invoice_get's lines.

rebillAmount.description: The line's corrected amount on the reissued invoice, for a Manual rebill.

rebillQuantity.description: The line's corrected quantity on the reissued invoice.

reason.description: Why, as the customer or the biller would say it.

rebillStrategy.description: How a CreditAndRebill reissues: CloneExact copies the lines, Rerate prices them again, Manual takes the rebill amounts you give. Defaults to CloneExact.

supportingDocumentIds.description: Documents on the invoice's shipments that support it, from document_list or shipment_get.

draftAdjustmentId.description: The draft adjustment, from invoice_list_adjustments or invoice_get_adjustment. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Credits, rebills or writes off receivables and books the entries that say so; only a person submits an adjustment, and the adjustment policy may still hold it for an approver.

tools.name: invoice_update_draft
tools.description: Change what a draft invoice says and where it goes: its memo, remittance instructions, email subject and body, recipients and attached documents. Only the fields you pass change; an empty string or list clears one. A posted invoice is changed with an invoice adjustment instead.

attachmentDocumentIds.description: The documents attached to the email, from document_list; replaces the list.

emailBcc.description: Who is blind-copied; replaces the list.

emailBody.description: The body of the email the invoice goes in.

emailCc.description: Who is copied; replaces the list.

emailSubject.description: The subject of the email the invoice goes in.

emailTo.description: Who the invoice is emailed to; replaces the list.

invoiceId.description: The invoice, from invoice_list or invoice_get. Never guess one.

memo.description: The note printed on the invoice.

remittanceInstructions.description: How the customer should pay, printed on the invoice.

policy.condition: Changing who the invoice is emailed to is a proposal a person decides; any other change runs once a person approves it.
policy.taintHold: Outside content could put its own wording or recipients on an invoice the customer receives.
policy.rationale: Edits a draft nobody outside has seen; the customer sees it only when a person sends it, but the recipients decide where it goes then.

tools.name: invoice_void
tools.description: Propose voiding an invoice. A draft is voided in place; a posted one through a full-reversal adjustment that credits it, which may wait for an approver. Its freight is rebilled or canceled as you say. Unapply payments and credits first. A person always decides.

disposition.description: Rebill puts its freight back on the billing queue to be billed again; DoNotRebill cancels it.

invoiceId.description: The invoice, from invoice_list or invoice_get. Never guess one.

reason.description: Why it is voided; kept on the invoice.

policy.rationale: Takes an invoice out of circulation and reverses what it booked; it cannot be undone, so only a person voids one.

tools.name: invoice_withdraw_dispute
tools.description: Withdraw an open invoice dispute the customer no longer pursues, without recording an outcome. The invoice's Disputed flag clears and it goes back to collections as it was. Use invoice_resolve_dispute instead when there is an outcome to record.

disputeId.description: The open dispute, from invoice_list_disputes. Never guess one.

note.description: Why the customer dropped it.

policy.taintHold: A withdrawal read from what a customer wrote is proposed, since it sends the invoice back to collections.
policy.rationale: Closes a dispute case inside Trenova with no outcome; it moves no money and a new case can be opened with invoice_open_dispute.

tools.name: ledger_cancel_journal_reversal
tools.description: Cancel a journal reversal that has not been posted, with the reason, when the entry should stand after all. The original entry is left as it is.

journalReversalId.description: The journal reversal, from ledger_list_journal_reversals or the result of ledger_create_journal_reversal. Never guess one.

reason.description: Why the entry should stand, in a sentence the requester can act on.

policy.taintHold: The reason is what the reversal's requester reads next, so a run that has read outside text proposes it.
policy.rationale: Withdraws a reversal before it reaches the ledger; nothing is booked, and it is requested again if it was needed after all.

tools.name: ledger_cancel_manual_journal
tools.description: Cancel a manual journal that is a draft, waiting for approval or approved but not posted, with the reason. It is kept, cancelled, and never posted. A posted journal is undone with ledger_create_journal_reversal instead.

manualJournalId.description: The manual journal, from ledger_list_manual_journals or ledger_get_manual_journal. Never guess one.

reason.description: Why it must not be posted, in a sentence its author can act on.

policy.taintHold: The reason is what the journal's author reads next, so a run that has read outside text proposes it.
policy.rationale: Withdraws a journal before it reaches the ledger; nothing is booked, and the entry is drafted again if it was needed after all.

tools.name: ledger_close_fiscal_period
tools.description: Propose closing a fiscal period once ledger_get_fiscal_close_blockers shows nothing in the way, so nothing more posts in it. Earlier periods must be closed first. A person always decides, and reopening it takes a reason.

fiscalPeriodId.description: The fiscal period, from ledger_list_fiscal_periods. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Ends posting to a period of the books a person signs off; only a person closes one.

tools.name: ledger_create_journal_reversal
tools.description: Propose reversing a posted journal entry that was booked in error, with every debit and credit swapped. It is dated the day you name, or the next open period's first day, waits for approval where the organization requires it, and ledger_post_journal_reversal books it.

accountingDate.description: The day the reversal is booked; a day in a closed period moves to the next open one where policy allows. A calendar day as YYYY-MM-DD, such as 2026-10-01.

journalEntryId.description: The posted journal entry to reverse, from ledger_list_journal_entries or ledger_get_journal_entry. Never guess one.

reasonCode.description: A short code for the kind of error, such as WrongAccount or Duplicate.

reasonText.description: What was wrong with the entry, as the approver and the auditor will read it.

policy.rationale: Commits the organization to taking a posted entry back out of the ledger, approved at once where approval is off; only a person requests a reversal.

tools.name: ledger_create_manual_journal
tools.description: Draft a manual journal entry for the general ledger: its lines, the accounts they post to and the day it is booked. It is saved as a draft and books nothing; ledger_submit_manual_journal sends it for approval. Take accounts from ledger_list_accounts and make the debits equal the credits.

accountingDate.description: The day it is booked to the ledger; it must fall in a fiscal period that takes manual journals. A calendar day as YYYY-MM-DD, such as 2026-10-01.

currencyCode.description: The ISO currency code, such as USD. Leave it out for the organization's functional currency.

description.description: What the journal records, as the approver will read it.

lines.description: The journal's lines, at least two, whose debits and credits must balance before it can be submitted.

credit.description: The credit as a decimal such as 125.00. Give a debit or a credit, never both.

customerId.description: The customer the line is for, from customer_list or customer_get, when it concerns one.

debit.description: The debit as a decimal such as 125.00. Give a debit or a credit, never both.

description.description: What the line is for.

glAccountId.description: The account the line posts to, from ledger_list_accounts; it must be active and allow manual journals.

locationId.description: The location the line is for, from location_list, when it concerns one.

reason.description: Why the entry is needed: the evidence or the correction it makes.

policy.taintHold: A journal drafted from what someone outside wrote is proposed, since its lines are what an approver books.
policy.rationale: Saves a draft journal inside Trenova; nothing reaches the ledger until a person submits, approves and posts it, and a draft is cancelled the same way.

tools.name: ledger_get_fiscal_close_blockers
tools.description: Say whether a fiscal period can be closed and list every blocker in the way. Blockers include unposted entries, earlier periods still open, subledger differences and accounting controls; nothing changes. Take the period's id from ledger_list_fiscal_periods.

fiscalPeriodId.description: The fiscal period's id, from ledger_list_fiscal_periods or the page you are on.

policy.rationale: Reads records the caller may already open; it changes nothing and sends nothing.

tools.name: ledger_get_journal_entry
tools.description: Retrieve one journal entry by id with its lines: the GL account each line posts to, its debit or credit, and the entry's source, approval and reversal history. Use ledger_list_journal_entries first when you have a number or a date.

journalEntryId.description: The journal entry's id, from ledger_list_journal_entries or the page you are on.

policy.rationale: Reads records the caller may already open; it changes nothing and sends nothing.

tools.name: ledger_get_manual_journal
tools.description: Retrieve one manual journal request by id with its lines, the account each posts to and its debit or credit. It also says who approved, rejected or cancelled it and why. Use ledger_list_manual_journals first when you have a number.

manualJournalId.description: The manual journal's id, from ledger_list_manual_journals or the page you are on.

policy.rationale: Reads records the caller may already open; it changes nothing and sends nothing.

tools.name: ledger_list_accounts
tools.description: List the chart of accounts: each general ledger account's code, name, type and status, with its balances when your data access reaches them. Use it to name the account a journal line posts to or to find an account by code. Filters: status (Active|Inactive); allowManualJe (boolean): accepts manual journal entries; text: accountCode, name; boolean: isSystem; date: createdAt. Dates: today, nextndays/lastndays with days, or YYYY-MM-DD; never Unix time.

filters.description: Conditions, combined with AND. Give value for a single comparison, values for in and notin, days for nextndays and lastndays, and nothing at all for isnull, isnotnull, today, yesterday and tomorrow.

limit.description: How many rows to return: 25 unless you ask, at most 50.

offset.description: How many rows to skip. When a result says hasMore, call again with its nextOffset for the next page.

query.description: Optional free text matched across the searchable columns. Omit it when you are filtering on a field.

sortBy.description: Field to order by. Defaults to most recently created.

sortDirection.description: asc for oldest or smallest first, desc for newest or largest.

policy.rationale: Reads records the caller may already open; it changes nothing and sends nothing.

tools.name: ledger_list_fiscal_periods
tools.description: List fiscal periods, the months, quarters or adjusting periods the books close by, with their dates and whether each is open, locked or closed. ledger_get_fiscal_close_blockers says what stops one from closing. Filters: status (Inactive|Open|Locked|Closed|PermanentlyClosed): Open accepts postings; Locked and Closed do not; periodType (Month|Quarter|Week|Adjusting); text: name; number: periodNumber; date: startDate, endDate; boolean: isAdjusting. Dates: today, nextndays/lastndays with days, or YYYY-MM-DD; never Unix time.

filters.description: Conditions, combined with AND. Give value for a single comparison, values for in and notin, days for nextndays and lastndays, and nothing at all for isnull, isnotnull, today, yesterday and tomorrow.

limit.description: How many rows to return: 25 unless you ask, at most 50.

offset.description: How many rows to skip. When a result says hasMore, call again with its nextOffset for the next page.

query.description: Optional free text matched across the searchable columns. Omit it when you are filtering on a field.

sortBy.description: Field to order by. Defaults to most recently created.

sortDirection.description: asc for oldest or smallest first, desc for newest or largest.

policy.rationale: Reads records the caller may already open; it changes nothing and sends nothing.

tools.name: ledger_list_journal_entries
tools.description: List general ledger journal entries, newest accounting date first, with their number, type, status, source reference and debit and credit totals. Narrow by status, source, fiscal period, an accounting date range or text in the number or description. ledger_get_journal_entry opens one with its lines.

fiscalPeriodId.description: Only entries in this fiscal period, by id from ledger_list_fiscal_periods.

fromDate.description: The earliest accounting date. A calendar day as YYYY-MM-DD, such as 2026-10-01.

limit.description: How many rows to return: 25 unless you ask, at most 50.

offset.description: How many rows to skip. When a result says hasMore, call again with its nextOffset for the next page.

query.description: Words to look for in the entry number, description or source reference.

referenceType.description: Only entries from this source, such as Invoice, CustomerPayment or DriverSettlement.

status.description: Only entries in this status.

toDate.description: The latest accounting date. A calendar day as YYYY-MM-DD, such as 2026-10-01.

policy.rationale: Reads records the caller may already open; it changes nothing and sends nothing.

tools.name: ledger_list_journal_reversals
tools.description: List requests to reverse posted journal entries, newest first, with the entry each reverses, its status, the day it books and why. Narrow by status to find reversals awaiting approval or approved ones still to post. Filters: status (Requested|PendingApproval|Approved|Rejected|Cancelled|Posted): Approved reversals are waiting to be posted; text: reasonCode, originalJournalEntryId; date: requestedAccountingDate, createdAt. Dates: today, nextndays/lastndays with days, or YYYY-MM-DD; never Unix time.

filters.description: Conditions, combined with AND. Give value for a single comparison, values for in and notin, days for nextndays and lastndays, and nothing at all for isnull, isnotnull, today, yesterday and tomorrow.

limit.description: How many rows to return: 25 unless you ask, at most 50.

offset.description: How many rows to skip. When a result says hasMore, call again with its nextOffset for the next page.

query.description: Optional free text matched across the searchable columns. Omit it when you are filtering on a field.

sortBy.description: Field to order by. Defaults to most recently created.

sortDirection.description: asc for oldest or smallest first, desc for newest or largest.

policy.rationale: Reads records the caller may already open; it changes nothing and sends nothing.

tools.name: ledger_list_manual_journals
tools.description: List manual journal requests, newest first, with their number, status, accounting day and totals, and whether they balance. Narrow by status to find drafts to finish, journals awaiting approval, or approved ones still to post. ledger_get_manual_journal opens one with its lines. Filters: status (Draft|PendingApproval|Approved|Rejected|Cancelled|Posted): Approved journals are waiting to be posted; text: requestNumber, description; date: accountingDate, createdAt. Dates: today, nextndays/lastndays with days, or YYYY-MM-DD; never Unix time.

filters.description: Conditions, combined with AND. Give value for a single comparison, values for in and notin, days for nextndays and lastndays, and nothing at all for isnull, isnotnull, today, yesterday and tomorrow.

limit.description: How many rows to return: 25 unless you ask, at most 50.

offset.description: How many rows to skip. When a result says hasMore, call again with its nextOffset for the next page.

query.description: Optional free text matched across the searchable columns. Omit it when you are filtering on a field.

sortBy.description: Field to order by. Defaults to most recently created.

sortDirection.description: asc for oldest or smallest first, desc for newest or largest.

policy.rationale: Reads records the caller may already open; it changes nothing and sends nothing.

tools.name: ledger_lock_fiscal_period
tools.description: Propose locking an open fiscal period while its books are reviewed for close, the step before ledger_close_fiscal_period. ledger_unlock_fiscal_period undoes it. A person always decides.

fiscalPeriodId.description: The fiscal period, from ledger_list_fiscal_periods. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Changes which dates the ledger takes postings for; only a person locks a period.

tools.name: ledger_open_fiscal_period
tools.description: Propose opening an inactive fiscal period so postings dated in it are accepted. Periods open in order, never in a closed fiscal year. A person always decides.

fiscalPeriodId.description: The fiscal period, from ledger_list_fiscal_periods. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Changes which dates the ledger takes postings for; only a person opens a period.

tools.name: ledger_post_journal_reversal
tools.description: Propose posting an approved journal reversal: it books the original entry's lines with debits and credits swapped and marks the original reversed. It changes account balances for good, so a person always decides.

journalReversalId.description: The journal reversal, from ledger_list_journal_reversals or the result of ledger_create_journal_reversal. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Books the reversing entry to the general ledger; only a person posts a reversal.

tools.name: ledger_post_manual_journal
tools.description: Propose posting an approved manual journal to the general ledger, in its fiscal period or the next open one the closed period policy allows. It changes account balances and is undone only by a reversal, so a person always decides.

manualJournalId.description: The manual journal, from ledger_list_manual_journals or ledger_get_manual_journal. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Books the journal's lines to the general ledger; only a person posts a manual journal.

tools.name: ledger_reopen_fiscal_period
tools.description: Propose reopening a closed fiscal period, with the reason, so a correction can post in it. Later periods must be reopened first and a closed fiscal year never is. A person always decides.

fiscalPeriodId.description: The fiscal period, from ledger_list_fiscal_periods. Never guess one.

reason.description: Why the period must take postings again: the correction and the evidence for it.

policy.rationale: Lets postings land again in books a person closed; only a person reopens a period.

tools.name: ledger_submit_manual_journal
tools.description: Submit a balanced draft manual journal for approval. It waits for an approver; where the organization has manual journal approval turned off, submitting approves it, so only a person does that. Read it with ledger_get_manual_journal first.

manualJournalId.description: The manual journal, from ledger_list_manual_journals or ledger_get_manual_journal. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Moves a draft journal into the approval queue inside Trenova; an approver decides and it books nothing until a person posts it.

tools.name: ledger_unlock_fiscal_period
tools.description: Propose unlocking a locked fiscal period so it is open again, when postings must still land in it before it closes. A person always decides.

fiscalPeriodId.description: The fiscal period, from ledger_list_fiscal_periods. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Changes which dates the ledger takes postings for; only a person unlocks a period.

tools.name: ledger_update_manual_journal
tools.description: Rewrite a draft manual journal before it is submitted: its description, reason, day, currency or lines. Fields left out keep their value; lines, when given, replace every line. Only a draft can be revised; a journal sent back by its approver is drafted again with ledger_create_manual_journal.

accountingDate.description: The day it is booked to the ledger; it must fall in a fiscal period that takes manual journals. Leave it out to keep it. A calendar day as YYYY-MM-DD, such as 2026-10-01.

currencyCode.description: The ISO currency code, such as USD. Leave it out for the organization's functional currency.

description.description: What the journal records, as the approver will read it. Leave it out to keep it.

lines.description: Every line of the rewritten journal, replacing the draft's lines. Leave it out to keep the lines as they are.

credit.description: The credit as a decimal such as 125.00. Give a debit or a credit, never both.

customerId.description: The customer the line is for, from customer_list or customer_get, when it concerns one.

debit.description: The debit as a decimal such as 125.00. Give a debit or a credit, never both.

description.description: What the line is for.

glAccountId.description: The account the line posts to, from ledger_list_accounts; it must be active and allow manual journals.

locationId.description: The location the line is for, from location_list, when it concerns one.

manualJournalId.description: The manual journal, from ledger_list_manual_journals or ledger_get_manual_journal. Never guess one.

reason.description: Why the entry is needed: the evidence or the correction it makes.

policy.taintHold: A journal rewritten from what someone outside wrote is proposed, since its lines are what an approver books.
policy.rationale: Changes a draft journal inside Trenova; nothing reaches the ledger until a person submits, approves and posts it, and a later revision changes it back.

tools.name: location_create
tools.description: Create a location record for a pickup or delivery address that has none, such as a facility read from a document. Look for it with location_list first; a person approves the new location before it is saved, and the code is assigned.

locationCategoryId.description: What kind of place it is, from location_list_categories: a warehouse, a customer site, a terminal.

name.description: The facility or company name at the address.

state.description: The two-letter US state abbreviation, such as TX.

policy.rationale: A new location is where colleagues will book freight, and its address is usually read from a document someone outside sent, so a person approves it first.

tools.name: location_get
tools.description: Retrieve one location by id, with its address, coordinates, geofence, timezone and category (appointments, parking, overnight). Use location_list first when you have a name, a code or a city.

policy.rationale: Reads records the caller may already open; it changes nothing and sends nothing.

tools.name: location_list
tools.description: List locations (facilities, terminals, yards) narrowed by status, code, name or city. maxTemperature.description: The highest temperature it may be carried at, in degrees Fahrenheit. Leave it out to keep it.

minTemperature.description: The lowest temperature it may be carried at, in degrees Fahrenheit, below maxTemperature. Leave it out for one setpoint such as a reefer held at -10 F, which is the maximum. Leave it out to keep it.

name.description: The commodity's name, unique in this organization. Leave it out to keep it.

stackable.description: Whether units may be stacked. Leave it out to keep it.

weightPerUnit.description: Pounds per unit. A decimal such as 42.5. Leave it out to keep it. Send an empty value to clear it.

widthPerUnit.description: Inches wide per unit. A decimal such as 42.5. Leave it out to keep it. Send an empty value to clear it.

policy.taintHold: A record read from a document or message someone outside sent is proposed, since colleagues book and pay against it.
policy.rationale: Changes a commodity inside Trenova; nothing is sent, and a later change puts it back.

tools.name: masterdata_update_hazardous_material
tools.description: Change a hazardous material: its class, UN number, packing group, shipping name, placarding, handling or emergency contact. Fields left out keep their value. Use masterdata_set_hazardous_material_status to activate or retire it.

class.description: The DOT hazard class or division. Leave it out to keep it.

description.description: What the material is. Leave it out to keep it.

emergencyContact.description: Who to call in an emergency. Leave it out to keep it. Send an empty value to clear it.

emergencyContactPhoneNumber.description: The emergency response phone number. Leave it out to keep it. Send an empty value to clear it.

ergGuideNumber.description: The Emergency Response Guidebook guide number. Leave it out to keep it. Send an empty value to clear it.

handlingInstructions.description: How it is handled. Leave it out to keep it. Send an empty value to clear it.

hazardousMaterialId.description: The hazardous material to change, from masterdata_list_hazardous_materials. Never guess one.

inhalationHazard.description: Whether it is a poison inhalation hazard. Leave it out to keep it.

isReportableQuantity.description: Whether it is a reportable quantity substance. Leave it out to keep it.

labelCodes.description: The label codes packages carry. Leave it out to keep it. Send an empty value to clear it.

marinePollutant.description: Whether it is a marine pollutant. Leave it out to keep it.

name.description: The material's name, unique in this organization. Leave it out to keep it.

packingGroup.description: The packing group: I is great danger, III minor. Leave it out to keep it.

placardRequired.description: Whether a vehicle carrying it must be placarded. Leave it out to keep it.

properShippingName.description: The proper shipping name from the hazardous materials table. Leave it out to keep it. Send an empty value to clear it.

quantityThreshold.description: The reportable quantity; required when isReportableQuantity. Leave it out to keep it. Send an empty value to clear it.

specialProvisions.description: The special provision codes, separated by commas. Leave it out to keep it. Send an empty value to clear it.

subsidiaryHazardClass.description: Any subsidiary hazard class. Leave it out to keep it. Send an empty value to clear it.

unNumber.description: The four-digit UN or NA number, without the prefix. Leave it out to keep it. Send an empty value to clear it.

policy.taintHold: A record read from a document or message someone outside sent is proposed, since colleagues book and pay against it.
policy.rationale: Changes a hazardous material inside Trenova; nothing is sent. What drivers placard and who they call follows it, so a person approves every change.
Names the plan the person approves the turn's proposals as. It writes no business record: the name is kept only as the plan's own title, beside the previewed changes the approval rests on.

tools.name: order_add_charge
tools.description: Add an order-level charge, one billed once for the whole order rather than on a shipment: a consolidation fee, a quoted flat rate. Give allocations only to split it among several payers; left out, the order's customer pays it all.

allocations.description: How the charge is split among payers.

amount.description: The share as an amount such as 250.00, when method is Amount.

billToCustomerId.description: The customer who pays this share, from customer_list. Never guess one.

method.description: Whether the share is a percent of the charge or a fixed amount.

percent.description: The share as a percent such as 60, when method is Percent.

amount.description: The amount, as a decimal such as 150.00.

description.description: What the charge is for, as the invoice line should read.

orderId.description: The order, from order_list, order_get or the orderId shipment_get shows. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Adds to what the customer is billed; nothing is invoiced or sent, and order_remove_charge takes it off until it is invoiced.

tools.name: order_attach_shipments
tools.description: Put shipments on an order so they are billed and tracked together. Each must be the order's customer's and neither canceled nor invoiced; a shipment on another open order moves off it, and an order it leaves empty is removed. A Billed or Closed order takes no more shipments.

orderId.description: The order to add them to, from order_list, order_get or the orderId shipment_get shows. Never guess one.

shipmentIds.description: The shipments to attach, from shipment_list or shipment_get.

policy.rationale: Regroups shipments under an order inside Trenova; nothing is sent, and order_detach_shipment moves one back out.

tools.name: order_cancel
tools.description: Cancel an order and every shipment on it that is not already canceled, with the reason the customer gave. An order with an invoiced shipment cannot be canceled; credit the invoice first. Canceling a shipment tells its carrier and trading partner as shipment_cancel would.

orderId.description: The order to cancel, from order_list, order_get or the orderId shipment_get shows. Never guess one.

reason.description: Why, as the customer said it.

policy.rationale: Cancels every live shipment on the order, which reaches carriers and trading partners; only a person cancels an order.

tools.name: order_close
tools.description: Close a Billed order once nothing more will be billed on it. Closing is final: a Closed order takes no more shipments or charges.

orderId.description: The Billed order, from order_list, order_get or the orderId shipment_get shows. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Settles an order for good; nothing reopens it, so only a person closes one.

tools.name: order_create
tools.description: Open a customer order: the commercial record that groups a customer's shipments and order-level charges under their PO or BOL. It starts as a Draft with its own number; attach shipments with order_attach_shipments and add charges with order_add_charge. Only from what the person or the customer asked for.

baseAmount.description: The base amount before accessorials, as a decimal such as 1250.00. An empty string clears it.

currencyCode.description: The ISO 4217 currency, such as USD. Defaults to USD.

customerId.description: The customer the order is for, from customer_list. Never guess one.

ownerId.description: The user who owns the order: the person who asked, or an ownerId order_get shows. Never guess one.

quotedAmount.description: What the customer was quoted, as a decimal such as 1250.00. An empty string clears it.

policy.rationale: Opens an empty order inside Trenova; nothing is billed or sent, and an order opened in error is canceled.

tools.name: order_detach_shipment
tools.description: Take one shipment off an order onto an order of its own, so it is billed on its own. The order's only shipment and an invoiced one stay where they are.

orderId.description: The order the shipment is on, from order_list, order_get or the orderId shipment_get shows. Never guess one.

shipmentId.description: The shipment to take off it, from shipment_get, shipment_list or the page you are on. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Moves a shipment onto a new order inside Trenova; nothing is sent, and order_attach_shipments puts it back.

tools.name: order_get
tools.description: Retrieve one customer order by id with the shipments it groups and its order-level charges, including which charges are already invoiced. Use order_list first when you have an order number, PO or BOL rather than an id.

orderId.description: The order's id, from order_list, the orderId on shipment_get or invoice_get, or the page you are on.

policy.rationale: Reads records the caller may already open; it changes nothing and sends nothing.

tools.name: order_list
tools.description: List customer orders, the commercial record that groups one or more shipments and their charges under a customer's order number, PO or BOL. order_get opens one with its shipments and charges. Filters: status (Draft|Confirmed|InProgress|Completed|Billed|Closed|Canceled): Billed means invoiced; Closed means nothing more will be added; text: orderNumber, poNumber, bol; number: totalAmount; date: createdAt. Dates: today, nextndays/lastndays with days, or YYYY-MM-DD; never Unix time.

filters.description: Conditions, combined with AND. Give value for a single comparison, values for in and notin, days for nextndays and lastndays, and nothing at all for isnull, isnotnull, today, yesterday and tomorrow.

limit.description: How many rows to return: 25 unless you ask, at most 50.

offset.description: How many rows to skip. When a result says hasMore, call again with its nextOffset for the next page.

query.description: Optional free text matched across the searchable columns. Omit it when you are filtering on a field.

sortBy.description: Field to order by. Defaults to most recently created.

sortDirection.description: asc for oldest or smallest first, desc for newest or largest.

policy.rationale: Reads records the caller may already open; it changes nothing and sends nothing.

tools.name: order_remove_charge
tools.description: Take a charge off an order before it is invoiced. An invoiced charge stays; credit its invoice instead.

chargeId.description: The order charge, from the charges order_get lists. Never guess one.

orderId.description: The order, from order_list, order_get or the orderId shipment_get shows. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Lowers what the customer is billed; nothing is invoiced or sent, and order_add_charge puts it back.

tools.name: order_set_charge_allocations
tools.description: Replace how one order charge is split among payers without touching the charge itself. Percents must add up to 100 and amounts to the charge; an empty list bills it all to the order's customer.

amount.description: The share as an amount such as 250.00, when method is Amount.

billToCustomerId.description: The customer who pays this share, from customer_list. Never guess one.

method.description: Whether the share is a percent of the charge or a fixed amount.

percent.description: The share as a percent such as 60, when method is Percent.

chargeId.description: The order charge, from the charges order_get lists. Never guess one.

orderId.description: The order, from order_list, order_get or the orderId shipment_get shows. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Moves who is billed for a charge; nothing is invoiced or sent, and the split is set back the same way until it is invoiced.

tools.name: order_update
tools.description: Change an order's customer, owner, PO number, BOL, currency, quoted amount or base amount. Send only what changes. Its status and total follow its shipments and charges and cannot be set here.

baseAmount.description: The base amount before accessorials, as a decimal such as 1250.00. An empty string clears it.

currencyCode.description: The ISO 4217 currency, such as USD. Defaults to USD.

customerId.description: The customer the order is for, from customer_list. Only an order with no shipments can change customer. Never guess one.

orderId.description: The order to change, from order_list, order_get or the orderId shipment_get shows. Never guess one.

ownerId.description: The user who owns the order: the person who asked, or an ownerId order_get shows. Never guess one.

quotedAmount.description: What the customer was quoted, as a decimal such as 1250.00. An empty string clears it.

policy.rationale: Edits an order's own fields inside Trenova; nothing is sent, and the old values are set back the same way. A changed amount is a money change.

tools.name: order_update_charge
tools.description: Change an order charge's description, amount or payer split. Send only what changes. An invoiced charge cannot be changed; adjust its invoice instead.

allocations.description: The whole new payer split; an empty list bills it all to the order's customer.

amount.description: The share as an amount such as 250.00, when method is Amount.

billToCustomerId.description: The customer who pays this share, from customer_list. Never guess one.

method.description: Whether the share is a percent of the charge or a fixed amount.

percent.description: The share as a percent such as 60, when method is Percent.

amount.description: The new amount, as a decimal such as 150.00.

chargeId.description: The order charge, from the charges order_get lists. Never guess one.

description.description: The new description, in full.

orderId.description: The order, from order_list, order_get or the orderId shipment_get shows. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Changes what the customer is billed; nothing is invoiced or sent, and the old amount is set back the same way until it is invoiced.
Publishes a document into the caller's own conversation, where only they read it.

tools.name: rate_amend_agreement_rules
tools.description: Propose changing an active rate agreement's lanes from a day: close out the lanes it replaces and add their successors, keeping the old rates in history. Take the lanes' ruleIds from rate_get_agreement. It changes what shipments are charged from that day, so a person always decides.

effectiveFrom.description: The first day the new lanes price shipments. A calendar day as YYYY-MM-DD, such as 2026-10-01.

lanes.description: The lanes, each priced through a formula template or a rate matrix.

destinationCity.description: The destination city, for a CityState destination.

destinationScopeType.description: How the destination is named. Defaults to Any.

destinationValue.description: The destination, read as originValue is.

direction.description: Whether the lane also prices the reverse haul. Defaults to Directional.

formulaTemplateId.description: The formula template that prices the lane, from formula_list_templates, with the lane's rate as its base rate. Give this or rateMatrixId.

hazmatOnly.description: Only hazardous freight rates on this lane.

label.description: A short name for the lane, such as Dallas to Atlanta.

maxCharge.description: The most the lane charges, as a decimal.

minCharge.description: The least the lane charges, as a decimal.

originCity.description: The origin city, for a CityState origin.

originScopeType.description: How the origin is named. Defaults to Any.

originValue.description: The origin for its scope type: a three-letter country code such as USA, a two-letter state code such as TX (for State and CityState), a postal code (Zip3, Zip5), a location from location_list, or a rate zone a lane of rate_get_agreement names. Leave it out for Any.

priority.description: Which lane wins when two match equally; higher wins.

rate.description: The lane's rate as a decimal such as 2.35, in what its formula template charges by.

rateMatrixId.description: The rate matrix that prices the lane, as a lane of rate_get_agreement names it. Give this or formulaTemplateId.

tempControlOnly.description: Only temperature-controlled freight rates on this lane.

rateAgreementId.description: The rate agreement, from rate_list_agreements or rate_get_agreement. Never guess one.

supersededRuleIds.description: The lanes this closes out, by ruleId from rate_get_agreement.

policy.rationale: Changes the rates an agreement prices shipments at; only a person amends a live contract.

tools.name: rate_apply_increase
tools.description: Propose a general rate increase or decrease on agreements' lane rates, by a percent or a flat amount, from a day. It moves every lane rate on the named agreements, one customer's or carrier's, or every active agreement of a party type. The old rates stay in history. A person always decides.

agreementIds.description: The agreements to move, from rate_list_agreements. When given, customerId, carrierId and partyType are ignored.

carrierId.description: Every active agreement with this carrier, from carrier_list. Ignored when agreementIds are named.

customerId.description: Every active agreement with this customer, from customer_list. Ignored when agreementIds are named.

effectiveFrom.description: The first day the new rates price shipments. A calendar day as YYYY-MM-DD, such as 2026-10-01.

flatChange.description: The change per rating unit, such as 0.10. Give this or percentChange.

partyType.description: Every active agreement of this party type, when no agreements, customer or carrier is named.

percentChange.description: The change in percent, such as 3.5 or -2. Give this or flatChange.

policy.rationale: Changes the rates many agreements charge customers or pay carriers; only a person applies a rate increase.

tools.name: rate_approve_agreement
tools.description: Propose approving a rate agreement in review, which is the moment it starts pricing shipments. A person always decides.

comment.description: A note on the review for whoever reads the agreement next.

rateAgreementId.description: The rate agreement, from rate_list_agreements or rate_get_agreement. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Turns on an agreement that prices what customers are charged or carriers are paid; only a person approves one.

tools.name: rate_archive_agreement
tools.description: Propose retiring a rate agreement for good. It is kept because its quotes point at it but never prices again. A person always decides.

comment.description: A note on the review for whoever reads the agreement next.

rateAgreementId.description: The rate agreement, from rate_list_agreements or rate_get_agreement. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Ends an agreement for good, which changes what customers are charged when it was active; only a person archives one.

tools.name: rate_commit_import
tools.description: Propose applying a reviewed rate sheet to its agreement from the import's day. The lanes it changes and drops are closed out, its new rates take effect, and the old rates stay in history. Read it with rate_list_imports first. It changes what shipments are charged, so a person always decides.

rateImportId.description: The rate import, from rate_list_imports. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Changes the rates an agreement prices shipments at; only a person applies a rate sheet.

tools.name: rate_correct_fuel_index_price
tools.description: Propose correcting a manual price on a custom fuel index that was entered wrong: its day or its price. A price fetched from EIA cannot be corrected. Every surcharge that follows the index prices from it, so a person always decides.

fuelIndexPriceId.description: The manual price, from rate_list_fuel_index_prices. Never guess one.

price.description: The price per gallon as a decimal such as 3.899.

priceDate.description: The day the price applies to, as the index publishes it. A calendar day as YYYY-MM-DD, such as 2026-10-01.

policy.rationale: Moves the price every fuel surcharge on this index is computed from, which changes what customers are charged; only a person sets it.

tools.name: rate_create_agreement
tools.description: Draft a rate agreement with a customer or a carrier from a rate sheet or a quote the person agreed: its code, name, dates, currency and lanes. It is saved as a draft and prices nothing until rate_submit_agreement sends it for review and a person approves it.

agreementType.description: The commercial arrangement. Defaults to Contract.

autoRenew.description: Whether it renews itself at its end.

carrierId.description: The carrier, from carrier_list, for a Carrier agreement.

code.description: A short code for the agreement, unique in the organization, such as ACME-2027.

currency.description: The ISO currency code it prices in. Defaults to USD.

customerId.description: The customer, from customer_list, for a Customer agreement.

defaultMaxCharge.description: The most any lane charges, as a decimal.

defaultMinCharge.description: The least any lane charges, as a decimal.

description.description: What the agreement covers.

effectiveFrom.description: The first day the agreement prices shipments. A calendar day as YYYY-MM-DD, such as 2026-10-01.

effectiveTo.description: The last day it prices shipments. Leave it out for an open-ended agreement. A calendar day as YYYY-MM-DD, such as 2026-10-01.

lanes.description: The lanes, each priced through a formula template or a rate matrix.

destinationCity.description: The destination city, for a CityState destination.

destinationScopeType.description: How the destination is named. Defaults to Any.

destinationValue.description: The destination, read as originValue is.

direction.description: Whether the lane also prices the reverse haul. Defaults to Directional.

formulaTemplateId.description: The formula template that prices the lane, from formula_list_templates, with the lane's rate as its base rate. Give this or rateMatrixId.

hazmatOnly.description: Only hazardous freight rates on this lane.

label.description: A short name for the lane, such as Dallas to Atlanta.

maxCharge.description: The most the lane charges, as a decimal.

minCharge.description: The least the lane charges, as a decimal.

originCity.description: The origin city, for a CityState origin.

originScopeType.description: How the origin is named. Defaults to Any.

originValue.description: The origin for its scope type: a three-letter country code such as USA, a two-letter state code such as TX (for State and CityState), a postal code (Zip3, Zip5), a location from location_list, or a rate zone a lane of rate_get_agreement names. Leave it out for Any.

priority.description: Which lane wins when two match equally; higher wins.

rate.description: The lane's rate as a decimal such as 2.35, in what its formula template charges by.

rateMatrixId.description: The rate matrix that prices the lane, as a lane of rate_get_agreement names it. Give this or formulaTemplateId.

tempControlOnly.description: Only temperature-controlled freight rates on this lane.

name.description: The agreement's name.

partyType.description: Whether it prices what a customer is charged or what a carrier is paid.

priority.description: Which agreement wins when two price a shipment; higher wins.

renewalNoticeDays.description: How many days before its end to warn about renewal.

policy.taintHold: An agreement drafted from a rate sheet or a message someone outside sent is proposed, since its lanes are what the organization will charge.
policy.rationale: Saves a draft agreement inside Trenova that prices nothing until a person approves it; rate_archive_agreement retires it.

tools.name: rate_discard_import
tools.description: Discard a rate sheet that was read and should not be applied, such as last month's file uploaded again. Its agreement is not changed.

rateImportId.description: The rate import, from rate_list_imports. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Closes a staged rate sheet inside Trenova without changing any rate; the sheet can be uploaded again.

tools.name: rate_duplicate_agreement
tools.description: Copy a rate agreement with its lanes, weight breaks, accessorials and fuel terms into a new draft, to start a renewal. The copy has none of the original's history or approvals; rate_update_agreement_draft then changes it.

code.description: The copy's code. Defaults to the original's with -COPY.

name.description: The copy's name. Defaults to the original's with (Copy).

rateAgreementId.description: The rate agreement, from rate_list_agreements or rate_get_agreement. Never guess one.

policy.taintHold: An agreement drafted from a rate sheet or a message someone outside sent is proposed, since its lanes are what the organization will charge.
policy.rationale: Saves a draft copy of an agreement inside Trenova that prices nothing until a person approves it.

tools.name: rate_explain
tools.description: Explain how a saved shipment's rate was arrived at: the agreement and rule that priced it and every charge with its arithmetic. It also shows what separated that rule from the others, a running total, any floor or ceiling that changed the number, and anything the engine warned about. Use it for "why is this priced at X", for a customer disputing a charge, and before quoting a similar lane. It reads the rating that actually produced the shipment's price, not a fresh one, so the figures match the invoice even after the contract has since changed.

shipmentId.description: The shipment whose rate to explain, from shipment_list or the page you are on.

side.description: Which side of the shipment to price: what the customer is charged, or what the carrier is paid. Defaults to Customer.

policy.rationale: Reads records the caller may already open; it changes nothing and sends nothing.

tools.name: rate_generate_confirmation
tools.description: Generate the rate confirmation for a move covered by an outside carrier. It is a new revision of the agreement, with the carrier's pay and the stops as they stand, rendered as a PDF and filed on the shipment. Generate after dispatch_create_carrier_assignment, or again after the rate or the stops change; a new revision voids the one before it. Nothing is sent: find the new revision with rate_list_confirmations and send it with rate_send_confirmation. A tender acceptance issues its own.

shipmentMoveId.description: The carrier-covered move, from dispatch_get_board (moveId) or shipment_get (its moves).

policy.condition: A first revision is generated as far as the agent allows; one that would void a revision already standing, which the carrier may hold or have signed, is a proposal a person decides, as is one the service would refuse or that cannot be read.
policy.rationale: Renders the agreement and files it on the shipment inside Trenova; nothing reaches the carrier until it is sent, and voiding the revision undoes it.

tools.name: rate_get_agreement
tools.description: Retrieve one rate agreement, a contract or tariff, by id with its lane rules, rates, minimums and weight breaks. It also gives the current version, the accessorial schedule and the fuel surcharge binding. rate_explain says how it priced one shipment. Take the id from rate_list_agreements.

rateAgreementId.description: The rate agreement's id, from rate_list_agreements, rate_explain or the page you are on.

policy.rationale: Reads records the caller may already open; it changes nothing and sends nothing.

tools.name: rate_get_matrix
tools.description: Retrieve one rate matrix by id: the grid of rates a lane rule prices from. It gives the axes (zone, zip, weight break, freight class and so on) and up to 200 cells with their keys, ranges and values. Take the id from a rule's rateMatrixId in rate_get_agreement.

cellOffset.description: How many cells to skip. When a result says cellsHasMore, call again with its nextCellOffset.

rateMatrixId.description: The rate matrix's id, from a rule's rateMatrixId in rate_get_agreement or the page you are on.

policy.rationale: Reads records the caller may already open; it changes nothing and sends nothing.

tools.name: rate_list_agreements
tools.description: List rate agreements, the contracts and tariffs that price freight for a customer or pay a carrier. Each has its code, name, party, type, status and effective dates. Narrow to a customer, a carrier, a status or text; rate_get_agreement opens one with its lane rules.

carrierId.description: Only this carrier's agreements, by id from carrier_list.

customerId.description: Only this customer's agreements, by id from customer_list.

limit.description: How many rows to return: 25 unless you ask, at most 50.

offset.description: How many rows to skip. When a result says hasMore, call again with its nextOffset for the next page.

partyType.description: Customer agreements price what a customer is billed; Carrier agreements price what a carrier is paid.

query.description: Words to look for in the agreement's code or name.

status.description: Only agreements in this status.

policy.rationale: Reads records the caller may already open; it changes nothing and sends nothing.

tools.name: rate_list_confirmations
tools.description: List a move's rate confirmations, newest revision first. Each shows the carrier, the revision, its status (Generated, Sent, Confirmed or Voided), who it was sent to and when, and whether and how the carrier confirmed it. At most one revision stands at a time; a new one voids the last. Use it before sending, voiding or recording a confirmation, and to find the revision rate_generate_confirmation made.

shipmentMoveId.description: The move, from shipment_get (its moves) or dispatch_get_board.

policy.rationale: Reads a move's rate confirmation revisions; the name a carrier typed when signing is left out, so nothing written outside the organization is read.

tools.name: rate_list_fuel_index_prices
tools.description: List the prices on file for one fuel index, newest first, with the day each applies to and whether a person entered it or it was fetched. Only a manual price on a custom index can be corrected, with rate_correct_fuel_index_price; rate_record_fuel_index_price adds the next one.

from.description: The earliest price day to include. A calendar day as YYYY-MM-DD, such as 2026-10-01.

fuelIndexId.description: The fuel index, from rate_list_fuel_surcharge_programs. Never guess one.

limit.description: How many rows to return: 26 unless you ask, at most 104.

to.description: The latest price day to include. A calendar day as YYYY-MM-DD, such as 2026-10-01.

policy.rationale: Reads records the caller may already open; it changes nothing and sends nothing.

tools.name: rate_list_fuel_surcharge_programs
tools.description: Read this week's fuel surcharge rate for every active fuel program. It gives the fuel index price and its date, and the surcharge as a rate per mile, a percent of linehaul or a flat amount. It says when a fallback price was used because this week's was missing.

query.description: Words to look for in the program's code or name. Omit for every active program.

policy.rationale: Reads records the caller may already open; it changes nothing and sends nothing.

tools.name: rate_list_imports
tools.description: List rate sheets uploaded against rate agreements, newest first, with the agreement and the day the new rates take effect. Each says how many lanes the sheet adds, changes and removes. A Parsed import waits for rate_commit_import or rate_discard_import.

limit.description: How many rows to return: 25 unless you ask, at most 50.

rateAgreementId.description: Only the imports against this agreement, from rate_list_agreements.

policy.rationale: Reads records the caller may already open; it changes nothing and sends nothing.

tools.name: rate_quote
tools.description: Price a shipment that has not been saved, from the customer's rate agreements and the organization's rating rules. Give the customer, the service type and the stops in order, each with a location id from location_list and a date. Returns the linehaul amount, the currency, which agreement and rule priced it, and whether a formula had to stand in because no agreement covered the lane. Nothing is saved: quote as many variations as you need before shipment_create.

asOf.description: Rate as of this date, YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to the first stop's date, then today.

customerId.description: The customer being billed, from customer_list.

stops.description: The stops in travel order: at least a pickup and a delivery.

date.description: The scheduled date, YYYY-MM-DD, or an RFC 3339 time.

policy.rationale: Reads records the caller may already open; it changes nothing and sends nothing.

tools.name: rate_record_confirmation
tools.description: Record that the carrier confirmed a rate confirmation outside its sign link, for instance by signing and returning the PDF or agreeing on the phone. The revision becomes the executed agreement and the carrier's assignment is confirmed. Record only a confirmation you were given, naming the person at the carrier who gave it; a revision already confirmed or voided cannot be confirmed. A carrier signing through the link is recorded on its own.

confirmedByName.description: The name of the person at the carrier who confirmed it.

rateConfirmationId.description: The revision the carrier confirmed, from rate_list_confirmations.

policy.rationale: Makes the revision the executed agreement to pay the carrier and confirms their assignment, on the word of someone outside the organization; voiding it afterwards withdraws the agreement rather than restoring it.

tools.name: rate_record_fuel_index_price
tools.description: Propose recording a published price on a custom fuel index, such as a customer's own index or a rack price the organization tracks. Every fuel surcharge that follows the index prices from it, so a person always decides. EIA indexes are fetched on their own and take no manual price.

fuelIndexId.description: The custom fuel index, from rate_list_fuel_surcharge_programs. Never guess one.

price.description: The price per gallon as a decimal such as 3.899.

priceDate.description: The day the price applies to, as the index publishes it. A calendar day as YYYY-MM-DD, such as 2026-10-01.

policy.rationale: Moves the price every fuel surcharge on this index is computed from, which changes what customers are charged; only a person sets it.

tools.name: rate_reject_agreement
tools.description: Propose sending a rate agreement in review back to draft, with what is wrong with it. A person always decides.

comment.description: Why, in a sentence the agreement's owner can act on.

rateAgreementId.description: The rate agreement, from rate_list_agreements or rate_get_agreement. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Returns an agreement to its author with the reviewer's reason; it prices nothing either way, but the review is a person's decision.

tools.name: rate_resume_agreement
tools.description: Propose putting a suspended rate agreement back in service without another approval round. A person always decides.

comment.description: A note on the review for whoever reads the agreement next.

rateAgreementId.description: The rate agreement, from rate_list_agreements or rate_get_agreement. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Turns an agreement back on so it prices shipments again; only a person resumes one.

tools.name: rate_run_simulation
tools.description: Replay past shipments against a rate agreement, usually a draft, to see what it would have charged or paid next to what they actually were. It runs in the background and changes no shipment and no rate.

description.description: What it is meant to answer.

name.description: What the simulation is called, such as Acme renewal against Q3.

partyType.description: Which side to replay: what customers are charged or what carriers are paid. Defaults to Customer.

rateAgreementId.description: The rate agreement, from rate_list_agreements or rate_get_agreement. Never guess one.

sampleFrom.description: The first ship day to replay. A calendar day as YYYY-MM-DD, such as 2026-10-01.

sampleLimit.description: The most shipments to replay. Leave it out for every shipment in the window.

sampleTo.description: The last ship day to replay. A calendar day as YYYY-MM-DD, such as 2026-10-01.

policy.rationale: Saves a simulation inside Trenova and replays past shipments in the background; no shipment, rate or invoice changes.

tools.name: rate_send_confirmation
tools.description: Email a rate confirmation to the carrier, with a link to sign it while it is unsigned. The PDF goes to the carrier's contacts that receive rate confirmations, or the carrier's own address. The recipients come from the carrier's record and cannot be chosen here; fix the carrier's contacts first if they are wrong. Send a revision that is Generated, Sent (to send it again) or Confirmed (the executed copy); find it with rate_list_confirmations.

rateConfirmationId.description: The revision to send, from rate_list_confirmations.

policy.rationale: Emails a binding agreement, with a link to sign it, to a carrier outside the organization; the recipients come from the carrier's record, and a sent email cannot be recalled, so a person decides every send.

tools.name: rate_submit_agreement
tools.description: Submit a draft rate agreement for review. It prices nothing until a person approves it. Read it with rate_get_agreement first.

comment.description: A note on the review for whoever reads the agreement next.

rateAgreementId.description: The rate agreement, from rate_list_agreements or rate_get_agreement. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Moves a draft agreement into review inside Trenova; it prices nothing until a person approves it.

tools.name: rate_suspend_agreement
tools.description: Propose suspending an active rate agreement, such as for a customer on credit hold, with the reason. Shipments stop rating against it at once; rate_resume_agreement puts it back. A person always decides.

comment.description: Why, in a sentence the agreement's owner can act on.

rateAgreementId.description: The rate agreement, from rate_list_agreements or rate_get_agreement. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Stops an agreement pricing shipments, which changes what customers are charged; only a person suspends one.

tools.name: rate_update_agreement_draft
tools.description: Rewrite a draft rate agreement before it is submitted: its header terms or its lanes. Fields left out keep their value. Only a draft is revised here; an active agreement's lanes change with rate_amend_agreement_rules. Read it with rate_get_agreement first for its lanes' ruleIds.

agreementType.description: The commercial arrangement. Defaults to Contract.

autoRenew.description: Whether it renews itself at its end.

code.description: A short code for the agreement, unique in the organization, such as ACME-2027.

currency.description: The ISO currency code it prices in. Defaults to USD.

defaultMaxCharge.description: The most any lane charges, as a decimal.

defaultMinCharge.description: The least any lane charges, as a decimal.

description.description: What the agreement covers.

effectiveFrom.description: The first day the agreement prices shipments. A calendar day as YYYY-MM-DD, such as 2026-10-01.

effectiveTo.description: The last day it prices shipments. Leave it out for an open-ended agreement. A calendar day as YYYY-MM-DD, such as 2026-10-01.

lanes.description: Every lane of the revised agreement, replacing its lanes: a lane with ruleId keeps that lane and changes only what it gives, a lane without one is new, and a lane left out is dropped. Leave it out to keep the lanes.

destinationCity.description: The destination city, for a CityState destination.

destinationScopeType.description: How the destination is named. Defaults to Any.

destinationValue.description: The destination, read as originValue is.

direction.description: Whether the lane also prices the reverse haul. Defaults to Directional.

formulaTemplateId.description: The formula template that prices the lane, from formula_list_templates, with the lane's rate as its base rate. Give this or rateMatrixId.

hazmatOnly.description: Only hazardous freight rates on this lane.

label.description: A short name for the lane, such as Dallas to Atlanta.

maxCharge.description: The most the lane charges, as a decimal.

minCharge.description: The least the lane charges, as a decimal.

originCity.description: The origin city, for a CityState origin.

originScopeType.description: How the origin is named. Defaults to Any.

originValue.description: The origin for its scope type: a three-letter country code such as USA, a two-letter state code such as TX (for State and CityState), a postal code (Zip3, Zip5), a location from location_list, or a rate zone a lane of rate_get_agreement names. Leave it out for Any.

priority.description: Which lane wins when two match equally; higher wins.

rate.description: The lane's rate as a decimal such as 2.35, in what its formula template charges by.

rateMatrixId.description: The rate matrix that prices the lane, as a lane of rate_get_agreement names it. Give this or formulaTemplateId.

ruleId.description: A lane already on the agreement, from rate_get_agreement, to keep and change; leave it out for a new lane.

tempControlOnly.description: Only temperature-controlled freight rates on this lane.

name.description: The agreement's name.

priority.description: Which agreement wins when two price a shipment; higher wins.

rateAgreementId.description: The rate agreement, from rate_list_agreements or rate_get_agreement. Never guess one.

renewalNoticeDays.description: How many days before its end to warn about renewal.

policy.taintHold: An agreement drafted from a rate sheet or a message someone outside sent is proposed, since its lanes are what the organization will charge.
policy.rationale: Changes a draft agreement inside Trenova that prices nothing yet; a later revision changes it back.

tools.name: rate_void_confirmation
tools.description: Void a rate confirmation so the revision stops standing and its sign link stops working. Voiding one the carrier confirmed returns their assignment to awaiting confirmation. Use it when the agreement as written is wrong and should not be signed; to correct it, generate a new revision instead, which voids this one. Say why in reason. Find the revision with rate_list_confirmations.

rateConfirmationId.description: The revision to void, from rate_list_confirmations.

reason.description: Why the agreement is withdrawn, in a sentence a person can check.

policy.condition: A revision the carrier has been sent or has signed is voided only as a proposal a person decides, as is one that cannot be read; one never sent is voided once a person approves it.
policy.rationale: Withdraws the organization's written agreement to pay a carrier, whose sign link stops working, and undoes a confirmation it carried; a voided revision cannot be restored, only replaced.

tools.name: receivable_apply_credit_memo
tools.description: Propose settling a customer's open invoices with a posted credit memo of theirs. Name each invoice and the amount of credit it takes; together they cannot exceed what is left of the memo, nor any invoice its open balance. A person always decides. Find the memo with invoice_list (billType CreditMemo).

accountingDate.description: The day it is booked to the ledger, usually today; it must fall in an open fiscal period. A calendar day as YYYY-MM-DD, such as 2026-10-01.

applications.description: The invoices the credit settles and how much goes to each.

amount.description: Applied to this invoice, as a decimal such as 250.00.

invoiceId.description: An open posted invoice or debit memo of the same customer, from invoice_list or receivable_list_open_items.

creditMemoId.description: The posted credit memo, from invoice_list or invoice_get.

policy.rationale: Uses a customer's credit to settle what they owe; only a person applies credit.

tools.name: receivable_apply_customer_payment
tools.description: Propose applying a posted payment's unapplied cash to that customer's open invoices. Name each invoice and the amount it takes, and any short pay to write off; together they cannot exceed what is unapplied. It books a ledger entry, so a person always decides. Find the payment with receivable_list_customer_payments and the invoices with receivable_list_open_items.

accountingDate.description: The day it is booked to the ledger, usually today; it must fall in an open fiscal period. A calendar day as YYYY-MM-DD, such as 2026-10-01.

applications.description: The invoices the unapplied cash pays and how much goes to each.

amount.description: Applied to this invoice, as a decimal such as 250.00.

invoiceId.description: An open posted invoice or debit memo of the same customer, from invoice_list or receivable_list_open_items.

shortPayAmount.description: Written off on this invoice as a short pay, if the customer will not pay it.

customerPaymentId.description: The posted payment, from receivable_list_customer_payments. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Moves a customer's cash onto their invoices and books the entry that says so; only a person applies cash.

tools.name: receivable_assess_late_charges
tools.description: Propose assessing late charges on overdue invoices as of a date, as one debit memo per customer. Each has a line per invoice and overdue period at the customer's rate, and no period is charged twice. Leave out customerIds to assess every customer. A person always decides.

asOfDate.description: The day overdue periods are counted to, usually today. A calendar day as YYYY-MM-DD, such as 2026-10-01.

customerIds.description: Only these customers, from customer_list or receivable_list_open_items.

policy.rationale: Bills customers for paying late; only a person assesses late charges, and the billing control may post the memos as they are raised.

tools.name: receivable_assign_collector
tools.description: Give a customer's overdue receivables to a collector, or take them off whoever has them. The collector must be a member of the organization and is told the account is theirs. Use a collectorId receivable_list_collection_worklist shows or the person who asked; leave it out only to leave the account with nobody.

collectorId.description: The collector's user id: a collectorId receivable_list_collection_worklist shows, or the person who asked. Leave it out to take the account off whoever has it. Never guess one.

customerId.description: The customer whose receivables these are, from receivable_list_collection_worklist, receivable_get_aging or customer_list. Never guess one.

policy.rationale: Changes who chases a customer inside Trenova and tells the new collector; nothing is sent to the customer and assigning someone else changes it back.

tools.name: receivable_get_aging
tools.description: Summarize accounts receivable aging: which customers owe money and how overdue it is, in current, 1-30, 31-60, 61-90 and over-90-day buckets. Each row names the oldest bucket holding a balance. Use receivable_list_open_items for the invoices behind a customer's balance and receivable_get_statement for their history. Amounts are named in withheldByAccess when your data access does not reach them.

asOf.description: The day to age as of. Defaults to today. A calendar day as YYYY-MM-DD, such as 2026-10-01.

customerId.description: Only this customer, by id from customer_list or a row of this tool.

limit.description: How many rows to return: 25 unless you ask, at most 100.

offset.description: How many rows to skip. When a result says hasMore, call again with its nextOffset for the next page.

overdueOnly.description: Only customers with a balance past due.

policy.rationale: Reads records the caller may already open; it changes nothing and sends nothing.

tools.name: receivable_get_bank_receipt
tools.description: Read one bank receipt with the customer payments that might be it, each scored out of 100, and its reconciliation queue entry. The score says how well a payment's reference, amount and date agree with the receipt. A receipt in Exception has no match yet; a score of 90 or more with a clear lead is what the system would have matched on its own. Use the id from receivable_list_bank_receipt_exceptions or the run's subject.

bankReceiptId.description: The bank receipt's id, from receivable_list_bank_receipt_exceptions or this run's subject.

policy.rationale: Reads a bank receipt whose memo the payer wrote; nothing changes and nothing is sent.

tools.name: receivable_get_statement
tools.description: Build one customer's account statement: invoices, payments and credits over a period with the running balance, what is still open, and their aging. It answers what a customer was billed and paid and what they owe now. Take the customer's id from customer_list or receivable_get_aging.

asOf.description: The statement date. Defaults to today. A calendar day as YYYY-MM-DD, such as 2026-10-01.

customerId.description: The customer's id, from customer_list, receivable_get_aging or the page you are on.

startDate.description: The first day of the statement period. Omit for the customer's whole history. A calendar day as YYYY-MM-DD, such as 2026-10-01.

policy.rationale: Reads records the caller may already open; it changes nothing and sends nothing.

tools.name: receivable_list_bank_receipt_exceptions
tools.description: List the bank receipts that could not be matched to a customer payment on their own and are waiting in the reconciliation queue. Each has its amount, the bank's reference and memo, why it was not matched, and the queue entry with who it is assigned to. Narrow with query to match the reference, memo or reason. Use receivable_get_bank_receipt for one receipt's candidate payments.

limit.description: How many rows to return: 20 unless you ask, at most 50.

query.description: Words to look for in the reference, the memo or the exception reason.

policy.rationale: Lists bank receipts whose memos the payers wrote; nothing changes and nothing is sent.

tools.name: receivable_list_collection_worklist
tools.description: List the collections worklist: overdue and disputed invoices ranked for a collector to chase, each marked Critical, Warning or Watch. Rows carry the customer, days past due, the open dispute's reason and the open amount. Use receivable_get_statement before calling a customer about their balance.

asOf.description: The day to rank as of. Defaults to today. A calendar day as YYYY-MM-DD, such as 2026-10-01.

limit.description: How many rows to return: 25 unless you ask, at most 100.

policy.rationale: Reads records the caller may already open; it changes nothing and sends nothing.

tools.name: receivable_list_credit_memo_applications
tools.description: List where credit memos were applied to the invoices or credit memos you name. Each application shows the amount and whether it still stands or was taken back; receivable_unapply_credit_memo takes one back.

invoiceIds.description: Invoices or credit memos, from invoice_list or invoice_get.

policy.rationale: Reads records the caller may already open; it changes nothing and sends nothing.

tools.name: receivable_list_customer_payments
tools.description: List recorded customer payments, newest first, with the amount, how much of it is applied to invoices, the method, the reference and the memo. Search by reference or memo text, narrow to one customer, or include reversed payments. Use it to find the payment a bank receipt represents when receivable_get_bank_receipt suggested nothing, and to see whether a customer's payment is already recorded before posting another.

customerId.description: Optional: only this customer's payments, by id from customer_list or a candidate's customerId in receivable_get_bank_receipt.

limit.description: How many rows to return: 20 unless you ask, at most 50.

query.description: Words to look for in the reference number or the memo.

status.description: Which payments to list. Defaults to Posted.

policy.rationale: Reads records the caller may already open; it changes nothing and sends nothing.

tools.name: receivable_list_open_items
tools.description: List the open receivables, the unpaid or partly paid invoices customers still owe, most overdue first. Each row has the due date, days past due, dispute and short-pay state, and the open balance. Narrow to one customer, a minimum number of days past due, or disputed invoices. invoice_get expands one.

asOf.description: The day to age as of. Defaults to today. A calendar day as YYYY-MM-DD, such as 2026-10-01.

customerId.description: Only this customer's invoices, by id from customer_list or receivable_get_aging.

limit.description: How many rows to return: 25 unless you ask, at most 100.

minDaysPastDue.description: Only invoices at least this many days past due.

offset.description: How many rows to skip. When a result says hasMore, call again with its nextOffset for the next page.

policy.rationale: Reads records the caller may already open; it changes nothing and sends nothing.

tools.name: receivable_match_bank_receipt
tools.description: Match a bank receipt to the posted customer payment it represents. The payment's amount must equal the receipt's exactly; the reference and date should agree too. Matching closes the receipt's reconciliation work item. Use the candidate from receivable_get_bank_receipt, or a payment found with receivable_list_customer_payments. When no payment has been recorded yet, use receivable_post_customer_payment with bankReceiptId instead.

bankReceiptId.description: The bank receipt, from receivable_list_bank_receipt_exceptions or the page.

customerPaymentId.description: The posted payment, from receivable_get_bank_receipt's suggestions or receivable_list_customer_payments.

policy.condition: Runs on its own only when the payment is the one posted payment with the receipt's exact amount and reference, and the amount is within the organization's money limits for agents; any other call waits for a person. The receipt it matches, if the run read it, does not hold it, because the receipt is read again from the organization's records; any other outside content does.
policy.rationale: Matches a bank receipt to a posted payment, closing its reconciliation.

tools.name: receivable_post_customer_payment
tools.description: Record a customer payment and apply it to that customer's invoices. Give the customer, the amount, the date and the method, and the invoices it pays with the amount applied to each; anything not applied stays on the customer's account as unapplied cash, which is right when you cannot tell which invoice a remainder pays. Give bankReceiptId when the money is an unmatched bank receipt: the amount must equal the receipt's, and the receipt is matched to the new payment. Only post against a customer you identified from the reference, the memo or the invoices, never from the amount alone.

amount.description: The payment amount as a decimal string, such as 1250.00.

applications.description: The invoices this payment pays and how much of it goes to each.

amount.description: Applied to this invoice, as a decimal string.

invoiceId.description: An open invoice of this customer, from invoice_list.

shortPayAmount.description: Written off on this invoice as a short pay, if any.

bankReceiptId.description: The unmatched bank receipt this payment records, from receivable_list_bank_receipt_exceptions or receivable_get_bank_receipt, to match it in the same step.

customerId.description: The paying customer, from customer_list or receivable_get_bank_receipt's suggestions.

memo.description: A note kept on the payment, such as the remittance text or why a remainder was left unapplied.

paymentDate.description: The day the money arrived; the receipt date for a bank receipt. A calendar day as YYYY-MM-DD, such as 2026-10-01.

paymentMethod.description: How it was paid. Defaults to ACH.

referenceNumber.description: The bank's reference, so the payment can be found again.
